headNote: Every run below ran on the workspace tree at branch head 890c725f, whose code is ccc25a83e319aebe7fdc0adc88037254c4a98474's: the commit above it adds only .legion/INFRA-750/implement.json. My red test sits above both.

implementerProof.how: Round 2's proof entry and both of its negative controls reproduce independently. The acceptance runs: 0 of 50 under -race (ok 527.203s) and 0 of 50 without it (ok 524.269s) of TestTwoStartsRaisingOneStreamAtOnceBothSucceed, and 0 of 20 of the 21-name acceptance-5 set under -race (ok 1295.588s), against its 1254.829s. The table test and the cluster test together, -race -count=10: ok 116.262s. Negative control 1 (its 'settle every refusal' regression), reproduced by changing `!overlapRefused(err)` to `err == nil` in a copy of the head tree: the rows `unanswered, and the stream does not hold it`, `refused otherwise` and `refused otherwise while the stream holds the update` all fail (`updateStream = <nil>, want nats: insufficient resources`). Negative control 2 (WithName removed), reproduced by dropping bus.WithName(t.Name()) from TestADrainEndsTheKVWatchersBeforeTheConnection in another copy: both subtests fail with the helper's new refusal. A third control of my own, the base's updateStream restored with the head's tests: 4 of the table's 8 rows fail and TestConcurrentUpdatesOfOneStreamEndWithTheStreamHoldingThem fails 3 of 3 (rounds 163, 25 and 124). The refactor of updateStream is behaviour-for-behaviour the round-1 loop: I checked each of the six cases against the old code, and the table now pins the sends and the reads of each.

failures.criterion: Acceptance 5 and the issue's Outcome: the clustered tests and the drain tests pass every run. The round-2 guard in warnOrErrorRecords (drain_kv_watcher_test.go:168-170) makes TestAStuckDeliveryStillEndsTheKVWatchers depend on a record nats.go logs asynchronously, so the set's pass is a race it wins today rather than a result the test guarantees.
failures.evidence: Measured, not reasoned: nothing a connected client logs carries its name. A probe of the drain tests' own start (bus.ConnectOwningStream with WithReplicas(1) and WithName(t.Name())) found 0 records naming the client after the start, after the bucket and in the instant Drain returned; the three that name it - `envoy nats disconnected`, `envoy nats connection closed`, `envoy nats recovery cancelled` - come from nats.go's close callbacks. Over 20 drains of TestAStuckDeliveryStillEndsTheKVWatchers' shape under -race, 16 had such a record when Drain returned and 4 did not, the first landing 1.629 ms, 1.989 ms, 2.045 ms and 2.254 ms later. That test (drain_hook_edges_test.go:238-249) reads the records with no wait of its own: between Drain and the read it makes one ConsumerNames round trip, and that round trip is the whole margin. The other two call sites sleep 200 ms and are safe today. The helper's comment states the opposite of what happens - 'a connected client logs at least its own `envoy nats connected`' - but that line is logged only by connectInBackground's ConnectedCB (connect.go:106-113), which a plain start does not use; so a reader cannot see the dependency either. The red test: `TestWarnOrErrorRecordsTakesAClientThatHasLoggedNothing` in packages/envoy/internal/bus/drain_kv_watcher_test.go, committed at bb93d7a9. It fails at this head - `go test -count=1 -run 'TestWarnOrErrorRecordsTakesAClientThatHasLoggedNothing$' ./internal/bus/` from packages/envoy gives `drain_kv_watcher_test.go:169: no captured record names "TestWarnOrErrorRecordsTakesAClientThatHasLoggedNothing", so this test's own client cannot be told from another test's: connect it with bus.WithName(t.Name())`, told to a test that did exactly that. The review's own second option fixes it with no race left: take the client's name from the caller, next to WithName (`warnOrErrorRecords(t, logs, name)`), and keep the refusal for a test that passes no name. Waiting for a naming record would also work but costs each drain test a wait. I ran TestAStuckDeliveryStillEndsTheKVWatchers 100 times under -race with both CPUs of this pod busy and it did not fail, so the race is real but not frequent here; CI's runners are not this pod.

The base's failing-first half, measured in round 1 at the same base 8a911ecc and unchanged by this round: 20 iterations of the set failed 8 (TestAStuckDeliveryStillEndsTheKVWatchers 7 times, TestTwoStartsRaisingOneStreamAtOnceBothSucceed once with this issue's message), and CI run 40857522211's envoy-go job is red on the same line at that commit.

measurements.what: The Outcome's second server, measured in round 1 on one-off clusters of three real nats-server binaries: v2.15.1 and v2.10.29 each started two programs at once at three copies, with 0 overlap refusals in 900 raw updates on v2.15.1 and 2 on v2.10.29. Round 2 changes updateStream's shape, not its sends or reads, and the table test pins both, so the measurement stands.

environment: The acceptance runs ran in the issue pod (2 CPUs) on the workspace tree before the red test was added. Every scratch tree and probe is under $TMPDIR/r2, outside the workspace, and is removed; `jj status` carries only my two commits.
notes: The round-2 implement handoff's trickyParts still says 'A client started without WithName also passes that way, which the helper's comment says'; round 2 is the round that stopped it passing. The code comment was corrected, the handoff line was not.

Unchanged from round 1, for the reviewer: an overlap-refused update is sent again as the caller built it, so a concurrent write that does not satisfy this caller can be overwritten. That is the write a server without the race takes after the other update, and the loop re-sends only while the stream, read again, does not hold what the caller asked for.
